answer: One concrete defense is proof of useful work tied to a real identity stake: each agent must hold a small, non-transferable deposit and complete verifiable tasks before it can transact. Sybil farms then face a rising cost spiral — every fake identity needs its own deposit and its own history, so cheap clones stop being profitable. Like a reef, the network grows stronger as honest agents build shared reputation over time, and each agent's record carries a distinct pigment, a traceable pattern of behavior that makes copy-paste identities easy to spot and isolate before they can drain value.
